canonical_question: Why was a single-crystalline bcc sample chosen with {100} faces specifically, rather than a polycrystalline aggregate or random orientations, for this study?

question_variants.question: Why was a single-crystalline bcc sample chosen with {100} faces specifically, rather than a polycrystalline aggregate or random orientations, for this study?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text describes the sample as a single-crystalline bcc sample with a cubic shape and {100} faces containing 128,000 atoms. It does not provide the rationale or justification for choosing this specific orientation or geometry over a polycrystalline aggregate.

answers.answer: The single-crystalline body-centered cubic (bcc) sample has a cubic shape with {100} faces and an edge length of around 13.5 nm (40 lattice constants); it contains 128 000 atoms. The text provides this description but does not explain why this specific geometry was chosen.
answers.conditions: MD simulation with periodic boundary conditions
answers.boundary_limitation: Rationale for geometry choice not provided.
evidence_spans: In the present study, we focus on the effect of chemical SRO on the vibrational density of states and the phonon heat conductivity in a prototypical refractory HEA, HfNbTaTiZr, which crystallizes in the bcc structure [3] , [43] , [44] . Using an atomistic model of this alloy, we are able to study, besides the random alloy, various degrees of chemical SRO in the alloy. As a result, we show that chemical SRO can modify the heat conductivity in a sizable way.
